opening_message:
Ticket 1: Alexander Brown (employee ID E018) requests admin access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E018.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Analyst (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Alexander Brown (E018) is a full-time Analyst. Requested admin to Payroll, but Payroll is owned by the Payroll Specialist role and analysts do not own it, so admin is not permitted. Maximum for this employee is write. Recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E018 as contractor with basic security training (HR note lists full-time; flagging discrepancy). Contractors max is read without advanced training; admin is never permitted. Requested admin exceeds max, so recommend read.
reason: Alexander Brown (E018) requested admin access to Payroll. Admin is never permitted: Payroll is owned by the Payroll Specialist role, not the Analyst role, and contractors are never allowed admin. The two notes conflict on employment type (HR: full-time Analyst → max write; Security: contractor with basic training → max read, with a flagged discrepancy). Since the contractor record with basic training only supports read, and read is the most restrictive level that does not exceed the maximum under either interpretation, I grant read.

- Security agent: employment type contractor, security training basic, recommendation read. Security DB shows contractor with basic training; contractors max is read without advanced training; admin never permitted; recommend read.

There's a discrepancy: HR says full_time, Security says contractor.

Access policy:
1. full_time employees: up to write. Admin only if employee's role owns the system.
2. contractor employees: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin.

Payroll is owned by Payroll Specialist role. Analyst does not own Payroll.

If full_time: max is write (no admin since not owner). Requested admin > max write, so grant write.
If contractor: max is read (basic training, not advanced). Requested admin > max read, so grant read.
